name: Philip Van Cortlandt
bio: A Representative from New York; born in New York, N.Y., on August 21, 1749; pursued classical studies; attended Coldenham Academy; engaged as a civil engineer; member of the New York Provincial congress, 1775; served in the Revolutionary War, entered as a lieutenant colonel; mustered out of the service with the rank of brigadier general for gallant conduct at the siege of Yorktown under General Marquis de Lafayette; delegate to the New York state ratification convention in 1788; served as supervisor of the town of Cortlandt, and as school commissioner and road master; member of the New York state assembly, 1788-1790; served in the New York state senate, 1791-1793; elected as an Anti-Administration candidate to the Third Congress and reelected as a Democratic Republican to the seven succeeding Congresses (March 4, 1793-March 3, 1809); engaged in agricultural pursuits; was a charter member of the Society of the Cincinnati; died on November 21, 1831, at Van Cortlandt Manor, Croton on Hudson, Westchester County, N.Y.; interment in Hillside Cemetery, Peekskill, N.Y.
